hello: Hey! The bowl's empty right now, which never happens. I've got a spare board if you want it.
first: First time in a bowl? Easy: you drop in off the coping, and {k:W} on the way down gives you speed. That's pumping.
Hit the wall fast and you fly. In the air: {k:J} kickflip, {k:K} grab, {k:A} {k:D} spin a 180. Just land with the board along the wall.
Next to the coping, or over the bar, {k:L} is a grind. A few tricks in a row without falling is a combo, and it multiplies. You've got one minute.
go: Take the red board. It's kind to people who respect it.
after: {score}! Not bad at all. Your best: {best}. Another one?
again: {score}. The bowl beats everyone at first. Your best is still {best}.
best: {score}?! New best! I'm sending this to the skate park group.
quit: The bowl isn't going anywhere. I'm here till they turn the lights off.
later: Cool. I'm here till they turn the lights off.

hello: Hi, welcome aboard Arkia-ish! I'm Gal, your flight attendant today. Sit anywhere you like, we're running a little late.
where: To Eilat! That was the plan, anyway. The captain said he knew a shortcut through Rishon's dunes, and here we are.
Honestly? Sea view, quiet, nobody kicking your seat. I'm in no hurry.
drink: Sure! Water, orange juice, or tea I made three hours ago. I'd go with the water.
And since you're a special passenger, have a pretzel too. Don't tell the others, there are none left.
safety: The exits are here, here, and... actually just here. One door is open, and the stairs are waiting outside.
In case of a landing on sand? We already landed on sand. So you're covered.
bye: Thanks for flying with us! Don't forget your things in the overhead bin, and come back any time.

c.saturday: "Saturday night at the City Hall square"

offer: The stage is almost empty. A man in a navy jacket runs across the square, phone to his ear, and stops right in front of Malul's drums.
Wait, wait, don't pack up! ...Yes, I'm on the line. Tell them I'm already there. ...No, not there. Here.
Raz, the mayor. Nice to meet you. Tonight I did a bar mitzvah, a community garden opening and the seniors' backgammon tournament. I lost. And now I'm here, and I missed the show of the year.
I know. I saw the page. Half the city posted a photo of whoever sat next to them. First time that page has posted anything that isn't about parking.
So I have an idea. Or a request. Or an idea that is really a request. Call the guys over?
huddle: Bro, the mayor? Really? I thought he was from the generator's insurance.

I know them too. Listen: what happened here tonight, religious, secular, grandmothers, skaters, all on the same square... I want it every month. A city event. A stage, chairs, real power. Not one generator and a prayer.
Every month? Like a steady workout. It hurts at first, then you can't do without it.
Bro, I'm filming this! ...No. I'm not filming. I swore. Just listening.
One thing. An event needs a name. All I've got are names like "Intergenerational Community Gathering, courtesy of the Culture Department". Save me.
name: dekel
A name matters. It's what people say when they invite someone else to come.
dekel
So what do you say?
rChair: "Bring a chair, bring someone." ...I feel like we stole that from a grandmother.
It's Savta Rachel's. She'll be happy. She'll say she isn't, but she will.
rSpirits: Four Spirits every month! Bro, I need a new drum skin.
The Culture Department will buy it. Write that down. ...Nobody's writing? Fine, I'll write it.
rSaturday: Saturday night. We start after Havdalah, so everyone can come. Those waiting for three stars, and those waiting for a parking spot.
Wow. That's exactly what my dad would say. Just with more verses.
lesson: And now a personal request. I always wanted to drum. When I was twelve my mother said: "Just not in the house." So here I am. Not in the house.
Okay, Mr Mayor. I play, you watch my hands, and our friend here holds the beat so we don't get lost. One, two, three, four.
lessonDone: Raz drums on a plastic chair. Not well, but with the joy of a man who waited forty years for it. His phone rings in the middle, and he doesn't answer. First time tonight.
Wallah, you've got a hand. The left one. The right one is still deciding.
Nobody tells me that in meetings.
plan: Right. Tomorrow morning I do a round: the Heichal, the Teder and the Great Synagogue. A stage, the youth and chairs. If everyone says yes, we have an event.
One small problem. My driver is at his grandson's bris. And I don't drive. Really don't. The city asked nicely.
You. We meet at the City Hall square. I'll bring coffee. ...I'll bring two, one always spills.
Drive slowly. He sounds like a man who spills coffee from a cup with a lid.

speechSpirits: Friends, neighbours, Savta Rachel. I'll be brief. ...I'm never brief, but I'll try.

speechSaturday: Friends, neighbours, Savta Rachel. I'll be brief. ...I'm never brief, but I'll try.

who: So who do I give it to? I'd give it to everyone, but it's one frame.
rMalul: Me? Bro... one, two, three... I've got no four. First time I've got no four.

c.ny: How is Rishon after New York?

hello: Hi! You look like someone who knows where the best coffee is. No? Okay, stay anyway.
ny: In New York everyone rushes to nowhere. In Rishon everyone stops to tell you you're not dressed warm enough. At thirty degrees.
And I love it. My neighbour brought me soup. Just because. On a Tuesday.
hair: Realest thing you'll see. In Brooklyn they called me "Traffic Light". Here I'm "the redhead from the Heichal". That's progress.
hero: Super Malul? Oh, the guy with the cape. Don't know him. At all.
Sarah looks away and smiles to herself.
bye: Bye, babe. I mean, bye. I say that to everyone. Sort of.

c.street: How is life on Natan Bernitzki?

hello: Hi! Sorry, I was waiting for the bus, then I remembered I don't know which one.
drive: Me? No. I tried once. The instructor got out in the middle of a junction and walked home. He said it was safer.
So I have friends with cars. And optimism.
street: Quiet, green, and the neighbours know everything about me. Even things I don't know yet.
bye: Bye! If you're driving towards... well, anywhere, tell me.

ori: Malul says this is the best bench in town. He's right, but don't tell him, it goes to his head.
I don't play. I'm the audience. Without an audience it's just four guys on a cliff.
Every day I say "five more minutes" and stay until the old tree is a shadow.

dudi: Super Malul! Who's that? Does she know you?

She doesn't look like all of them.
Dudi is right. Malul keeps that to himself.
ask: So: I know who you are. You know who I am. And nobody else knows anything.
Want to be... a secret? Just the two of us?
rYes: Deal. I'll be the girl at the side who smiles when you save someone. And nobody will get why.
She kisses his cheek, right by the mask, and laughs.
rShy: OMG, a blushing superhero. Cutest thing I've seen in Israel.
Yes. That's a yes. We're a secret.
tower: The old water tower at night. Sarah climbs the low fence and looks at the lights of Rishon.
New York has the Empire State. Here there's a hundred-year-old water tower and no queue. I like this better.

optician: Optician! My glasses are round, and they must stay round. Last time they tried to sell me square ones. I ran.

bank: Bank. I need one signature. One.

The clerk said come tomorrow. But she gave me a sweet, so it worked out.
bakery: Zohar! Challah as usual? And cookies for Savta?

market: Zohar comes out with two bags, a watermelon and a pot plant. She forgot the milk.

thanks: Thank you. Really. Without a car this city is three times bigger.
rAgain: You'll regret saying that. I have a list for next week too. And the one after.
rLessons: What if I teach you to drive?
Brave. My last instructor moved to a moshav. But... okay. Sunday. In an empty car park. Completely empty.

c.tip: Any tip for a good party?

hello: Hold on, just closing with the DJ. ...Yes, honey, eight thirty and not a minute later. Great. Hi! Are you here for a wedding or a party?
job: I'm Sapir. Weddings, bar mitzvahs, birthdays, bachelorette parties. If anyone danced in Rishon, chances are I set up their dance floor.
The secret? Know who isn't talking to whom, and seat them as far apart as possible. Then, at the end of the night, they dance together. Every time.
jeep: Black, tall and full to the roof. Three hundred cups, two speakers, a balloon arch and one bride's mother left over from Tuesday.
Sapir taps the jeep's roof, and something inside falls over.
It's fine. That was the number-two balloon.
tip: Three things. Food before the dancing, not after. Air conditioning on twenty-two, not lower. And put the crazy uncle next to the speaker, so he feels important.
No money for a hall? A garden in Nahalat Yehuda, a string of lights and the whole street comes. Best party there is.
bye: Right, I have a wedding at the Laguna at seven. If you see a black jeep going fast, that's me, and it's because of the desserts.

hello: The harvest has started and my hands are not what they were. Got young legs? I have an empty barrel and sun over the vineyard.
introFirst: Very simple. Grapes fall, you move the barrel and catch them. A golden grape is worth three. And if you see a bee, move. It doesn't complain, it stings.
after: {score} points! That's holiday wine. Your best: {best}.
best: {score}! A new record! I'm writing it on the barrel, next to the Baron's name.
about: The oldest winery in the country, since the Baron. Once the whole colony worked here. Today it's me, the bees and whoever passes by.
bye: L'chaim! I mean, goodbye. Here it's the same thing.

hello: In 1882 they dug the sand here for weeks, until someone shouted "We found water!". Want to try? I have a hoe.
introFirst: You dig a hole and the colour says how close you are. Blue is very close, green is damp, brown is desert. You have ten digs. Not in my garden.
intro: The hoe is waiting. Ten digs.
after: {score} points. That's how a colony was built. Your best: {best}.
best: {score}! A new record! Had you been here in 1882, they'd have named a street after you.
about: It's the city's motto. "We found water", like in the Bible. Without that water there'd be no Rishon, no winery and nowhere for me to put this chair.
bye: Drink water, sweetie. Here that's respect.

hello: Bro, my partner went for an ice lolly an hour ago. Want a bat?
introFirst: Simple. When the ball reaches your circle, press Space. Right on time is perfect. Three misses and it's over. Nobody counts except me.
after: {score} hits! A Rishon rally. Your best: {best}.
best: {score}! A new record! The whole beach heard the tok-tok.
about: Rule one: nobody wins at matkot. Only who keeps going. Rule two: don't drop it on the neighbour's towel.
bye: Take care. And bring an ice lolly if you see my partner.
